input: Add a dark mode toggle to the settings page of my existing React app.

tasks.title: Read me first: assumptions and gaps
tasks.description:
This plan is a starting point and may still have gaps. Read the items below before relying on it.
The dates are suggestions meant to keep momentum. Moving one is normal, and overdue cards simply show in red.
Pacing assumed: about 10 hours a week, starting Mon 26 Oct (you did not say how much time you have). If you add your hours per week or a start date to the description and generate again, the dates will follow.
checklist: Assumption, verify: The existing app uses standard CSS or CSS modules, so CSS custom properties can be layered on top without conflict How to check: Open the app's existing stylesheet files and check whether they use plain CSS, CSS modules, or a CSS-in-JS library
Assumption, verify: The settings page already exists as a component and can accept new UI elements How to check: Find the settings page component file in the codebase and confirm it renders normally
Assumption, verify: localStorage is available in the browsers the app targets How to check: Check the app's browser support requirements; localStorage is unavailable in some private-browsing modes
For any price, rate or rule above: check the vendor or official source directly, or ask a professional for anything legal or financial.
tasks.notes:
NOT MENTIONED IN YOUR DESCRIPTION (often matters):
- No mention of whether the app already has a global state manager (Context, Redux, Zustand) that the theme should plug into
- No mention of whether the app should also detect and respect the user's OS-level dark mode preference on first visit

tasks.title: Decisions needed: choices only you can make
tasks.description: These choices were not in your description, so they are yours to make. Each has a recommended default: accept it and move on, or swap it for your own.
checklist: Should the app automatically match the user's OS dark/light preference on their first visit before they set a preference? Options: Yes, use the prefers-color-scheme media query as the default / No, always start in light mode. Recommended default: Yes, use the prefers-color-scheme media query as the default.

Where should the theme state live? Options: A new React Context so any component can read the current theme / Local state in the settings page component only (simpler, but other components cannot react to it). Recommended default: A new React Context so any component can read the current theme.
Recommended default for styling: CSS custom properties (variables) for theme switching. Why: Works with any existing CSS setup, no extra library needed
Recommended default for state persistence: localStorage. Why: Simple, zero-dependency way to remember a UI preference across sessions

tasks.title: Define dark and light theme tokens with CSS custom properties
tasks.description:
Create two sets of CSS colour and style variables, one for light mode and one for dark mode, applied via a data attribute on the root element.
Why this matters: All components read from these variables, so the whole app switches theme by changing one attribute.
checklist: Create or update a global CSS file with :root variables for light mode colours (background, text, borders, etc.)
Add a [data-theme='dark'] block with overriding dark mode values for the same variable names
Check existing components use colours only from these variables, or update a few key ones as a test
tasks.notes: CSS custom properties: CSS variables written as --name: value that any rule can reference with var(--name). data-theme attribute: a custom HTML attribute set on the <html> or <body> tag to switch the active variable set.

tasks.title: Build a theme context and hook
tasks.description:
Depends on: Define dark and light theme tokens with CSS custom properties
Create a React Context that holds the current theme value and a function to toggle it, reading from and writing to localStorage for persistence.
Why this matters: Any component in the app can read or change the theme without prop-drilling.
checklist: Create a ThemeContext file that initialises theme from localStorage, falling back to the OS preference (or light mode, per your decision)
Expose a toggleTheme function that flips the value and saves it to localStorage
Apply data-theme attribute to the <html> element whenever the theme value changes
Wrap the app's root component with the new ThemeProvider so all pages can access it
tasks.notes: React Context: a built-in React feature that shares a value with any child component without passing it through every level. localStorage: browser storage that survives page refreshes.

tasks.title: Add the dark mode toggle to the settings page
tasks.description:
Depends on: Build a theme context and hook
Place a toggle switch on the existing settings page component that reads the current theme and calls toggleTheme when clicked.
Why this matters: This is the visible control the user interacts with.
checklist: Import and use the theme hook inside the settings page component
Add a labelled toggle or checkbox element bound to the current theme value
Call toggleTheme on change and confirm the page switches colour immediately
Ensure the toggle label clearly indicates the current state (e.g. Dark mode: on/off)

tasks.title: Test and polish the dark mode feature
tasks.description:
Depends on: Add the dark mode toggle to the settings page
Manually verify the toggle works across the app, the preference persists after a page refresh, and no existing components look broken in dark mode.
Why this matters: Catches styling gaps before real users see them.
checklist: Toggle dark mode and visually check every main page or component for unreadable text or clashing colours
Refresh the page and confirm the chosen theme is restored
Open the app in a private window and confirm the default theme matches your decision
Fix any components that still use hard-coded colours instead of CSS variables
